This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed to set aside the judgment and decree passed in MCOP No.423 of 2014, dated 14/11/2017 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special Sub Court),
Madurai.

Madurai

sentences.text: 2.The facts in brief:-
On 30/04/2013 at about 11.40 am, the petitioner along with his wife and relatives was travelling in an Auto bearing registration No.TN-58-X-5592 on the Madurai- Theni main road by keeping left.
When the Auto was nearing the occurrence place, a parked vehicle (TATA SUMO) bearing registration No.TN-67-U-6162 was taken in a rear direction without making any signal by its driver.
It hit the front side portion of the Auto.
The petitioner suffered various injuries on his body.
He was taken to Madurai Rajaji Government Hospital after taking first aid.
Later, he was referred to a private hospital called 'Devadas Hospital' and he was in patient from 30/04/2013 to 12/05/2013.
There was fracture on his left thigh region.
He underwent surgery.
After that, he was taking continuous treatment because of the accidental injuries.
Now he suffered partial permanent disability and could not continue his work as before.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
3.Over the occurrence, a case in Crime No.87 of 2013 was registered for the offences under sections 279 and 337 IPC against the driver of the offending vehicle.
He admitted his guilt and paid the fine amount before the Judicial Magistrate Court, Usilampatti.
He was running a mechanical work shop and because of the accidental injuries, as mentioned above, he could not continue his work as before.
So there is income loss also.
4.That was resisted by the 2nd and 4th respondents.
5.The 2nd respondent stated in its counter that the occurrence occurred only due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the Auto driver TN-58-X-5592.
He only hit the TATA SUMO behind.
So the 2nd respondent is not liable to pay the compensation on the behalf of the 1st respondent.

6.The 4th respondent filed a counter stating that the policy for the vehicle TN-58-X-5592 was insured with them only after 25/11/2015; With regard to the negligent aspect, it supported the case of the claimant.
7.Before the Tribunal, on the side of the claimant, one witness was examined and 16 documents marked.
On the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis side of the respondents, no oral and documentary evidence was adduced.

Disability Certificate of the petitioner was marked as Ex.C1.

8.At the conclusion of the enquiry, the Tribunal recorded a finding of fact that the accident took place because of the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle bearing registration No.TN-67- U-6162.
It also relied upon the admission of guilt made by the driver of the offending vehicle.
By relying upon this document, it recorded a finding of fact, which is not disputed by the respondents herein.
So, that portion of the order is confirmed.
9.Seeking enhancement of compensation only, this appeal has been preferred.

10.The learned counsel appearing for the appellant would submit that the claimant suffered partial permanent disability; Being a mechanical work shop owner, his physical fitness is required for carrying on his avocation.
Because of the accidental injuries, he suffered 100% loss of earning capacity.
On that account, he wants the matter to be considered for enhancement.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
11.The
Tribunal has recorded a finding that the claimant was a mechanic by profession based upon Ex.B16.
From the medical records, it was found that he suffered fracture on the left and right hand portion.
From this, it is seen that he suffered multiple fracture.
He underwent surgery in a private hospital as in patient as noted above.
He was referred to Medical Board attached to the Government Rajaji Hospital, Maudrai.
It assessed the disability at 45%.
By adopting percentage basis, the Tribunal awarded Rs.1,80,000/- towards partial permanent disability.
12.The following tabulation shows the categorisation of the compensation.

S.No. Head   01. Disability (45% x 4000) Rs.1,
 02. Pain and suffering Rs.
03 . Loss of earning capacity during Rs.
treatment period

04. Extra Nourishment Rs. 
 05.
Attendant charges Rs.
06. Damages to clothing and articles Rs.
07 . Transport to hospital Rs.

08. Medical expenses Rs 2,
 Total Rs.4,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 13.As mentioned above, the claimant wants enhancement of compensation on the basis of the partial permanent disability.
But absolutely, no evidence is placed before this court that because of the accidental injuries, he closed his Mechanic Shop and was not able to earn as before.
So, the earning capacity of the claimant is not affected due to the accident.

I find absolutely no reason to differ,
which in my considered view of this court, the compensation is just compensation.
